name: icey (HTTP server module)
workload: wrk -t4 -c100 -d10s against an empty-body 200 OK handler on one vCPU: icey single-threaded HTTP/1.1 keep-alive server versus a Go net/http keep-alive server (Node.js v20 and a hand-rolled libuv+llhttp C server also measured).
claimed_speedup: Keep-alive: icey 72,209 req/s at 1.43 ms average latency versus Go 1.25 net/http 53,878 req/s at 2.31 ms (README: 'outperforms Go's net/http by 34%'), Node.js v20 45,514 req/s at 3.56 ms, raw libuv+llhttp 96,088 req/s at 1.04 ms. Connection: close is parity: icey 14,330 req/s versus Go 14,723 req/s (Go marginally ahead), Node.js 9,309 req/s, raw libuv 18,468 req/s.
compiler_and_flags: C++ compiler not stated; built with cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_PERF=ON -DENABLE_LOGGING=OFF. Baselines: go1.25.0, Node v20.19.5, wrk 4.1.0 [epoll]. Harness: src/http/perf/benchmark.sh, httpperf.cpp, go-server.go, node-server.js.
hardware: 11th Gen Intel Core i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz, 1 vCPU, Linux 6.8.0-106-generic x86_64
tradeoffs: Single-threaded libuv loop per server; multi-core scaling is one server per core with SO_REUSEPORT (the 'multi' variant, not part of the quoted comparison). LGPL-2.1+ licence. C++20. The HTTP module is one of about 16 modules (WebRTC via libdatachannel, TURN, Symple signalling, FFmpeg pipeline).
caveats: First-party benchmark with public harness and CPU stated, but the C++ compiler is not named, so it falls short of tier A. Server and wrk share the single vCPU, so the load generator competes with the server; one run, no variance reported. The handler returns an empty 200 with no routing, TLS or body, so this measures per-request framework overhead only. With Connection: close the claim disappears (Go 14,723 versus icey 14,330 req/s). Go server runs default net/http with goroutine-per-connection and no tuning. The project's headline claim ('lightweight libwebrtc alternative', media stack) has no numeric comparison: the README table against libWebRTC, libdatachannel and GStreamer is qualitative (build time 'Hours' versus 'Minutes', binary size '50MB+' versus 'Small'). This record therefore documents the HTTP module, not the media path; the listed baseline libwebrtc has no numbers.
